deep.reconstruction:
This page is from lecture notes for a talk ('laïus') on the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, dated Nov.–Dec. 1966.

Setting (from the previous page). X is a non-singular algebraic variety over C with the Zariski topology. The previous page set up the natural map from the algebraic hypercohomology H^*(X, Ω^•_X) to the analytic hypercohomology H^*(X^an, Ω^•_{X^an}). By the holomorphic Poincaré lemma, the latter equals H^*(X^an, C).

Theorem. This map is an isomorphism for X smooth and locally of finite type over C.

Reduction to the affine case. If X is affine, the Ω^p_X are quasi-coherent on an affine scheme, so H^q(X, Ω^p) = 0 for q > 0. The hypercohomology is then just the cohomology of the complex of global algebraic differential forms Γ(X, Ω^•).

Corollary. For X affine and smooth, H^*(X^an, C) is computed by the global algebraic de Rham complex.

N.B. Conversely, the general theorem follows from the affine case. One uses the Mayer–Vietoris/Čech (Leray) spectral sequence of an affine open cover, comparing algebraic and analytic sides term by term. Finite intersections of affines are affine if X is separated.

Sketch of proof, proper case. If X is proper, compare the two Hodge-to-de Rham ('Frölicher') spectral sequences E_1^{pq} = H^q(X, Ω^p) ⇒ H^{p+q}:
- the algebraic one;
- the analytic one.
GAGA gives an isomorphism on the E_1 terms, hence on the abutments. Grothendieck remarks that this case was 'essentially known since Serre's GAGA'.

Sketch of proof, general case. The general (affine smooth) case needs a stronger tool than GAGA: Hironaka's resolution of singularities. One embeds X in a smooth proper X̄ whose boundary is a normal crossing divisor D. One then compares:
- algebraic forms on X with forms with poles (logarithmic or meromorphic) along D;
- these in turn, analytically, with C on X^an.
The lecturer intends to 'give an idea of the principles of the proof of the comparison theorem'.

Section 4, 'metaphysical consequences'. Complex cohomology, defined transcendentally, is interpreted as de Rham cohomology. This gives it a purely algebraic description that makes sense for smooth schemes over any field. It carries a filtration (the Hodge filtration) whose graded pieces are the E_∞ terms of the spectral sequence. The next page then criticises algebraic de Rham cohomology in characteristic p, motivating crystalline cohomology.

All of this is the content of Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966), originating in his 1963 letter to Atiyah.
errors: As transcribed, the theorem is stated for X a (pre)scheme locally of finite type over C, without the word 'smooth'. The statement is false for singular X: there one needs Hartshorne's de Rham cohomology via formal completion of an embedding. Smoothness is implicit from the previous page ('non singulières'), and the corollary explicitly says 'non sing.'.

The reduction from the general case to the affine case via a Čech/Leray spectral sequence is cleanest when X is separated, so that intersections of affines are affine. Otherwise one needs an extra induction. This is a minor gap, consistent with the previous page's 'X est supposé séparé'.

The phrase 'le cas général se réduit au cas affine, lisse, avec des moyens plus puissants que Gaga' slightly conflates two steps. The reduction to the affine case is elementary. Resolution of singularities is used to prove the affine (non-proper) case via a good compactification.

ideas.what: Comparison isomorphism between algebraic de Rham hypercohomology and singular cohomology of X^an for smooth complex varieties
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham comparison theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1963 letter to Atiyah; Publ. IHES 29, 1966)
ideas.where_published: Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966), 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties'

ideas.what: Proper case via GAGA applied to the E_1 terms of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences
ideas.modern_name: GAGA plus comparison of Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences

ideas.what: Non-proper case via Hironaka resolution: a normal crossing compactification and forms with poles along the boundary
ideas.modern_name: Comparison via good compactification and meromorphic/logarithmic forms (later Deligne's log de Rham complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1966; refined by Deligne (Équations différentielles, Hodge II)

ideas.what: 'Metaphysical' consequence: transcendental cohomology acquires an algebraic, field-independent description with a Hodge filtration, as a starting point for p-adic/crystalline theory
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham cohomology as a Weil-cohomology candidate; motivation for crystalline cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck ('Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés 1968)
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a lecture outline restating Grothendieck's published 1966 comparison theorem and its standard proof sketch (GAGA in the proper case, Hironaka in general). Nothing new beyond the anecdotal reference to private 'papier bleu' notes and the remark that the proper case was essentially known since GAGA.
transcription_corrections: 'des suites spectrales de type ∞' is more likely 'de type (*)', referring to the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence (*) of the previous page; the next page also mentions 'une suite spectrale (*)'.
The crossed-out word before 'schéma' is probably 'pré-' (préschéma), and the struck word after 'fini' may be 'lisse' or 'séparé'. Smoothness is intended.

'Je prouve dans papier bleu' likely means a pointer to Grothendieck's separate blue-paper notes ('Je prouve' perhaps misread for 'Je prouve'/'Preuve'). The same 'papier bleu' is referenced on the next page.
